gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-thai-lo: Nulshock stretches out wide and technical, its outlined capitals barely taller than the lowercase. And Noto Sans Thai Looped sits underneath with tall, sturdy-looking lowercase, a fine partner unless the heading is shrunk down to its size.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-tifinag: Wide, bold and wire-drawn, Nulshock traces every letter with one steady line. But Noto Sans Tifinagh fills its lines with puffed-up, rounded bowls, so the thin outline up top and the inflated shapes below keep each other interesting.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Noto Sans Tirhuta reads big and contemporary, with a dominant x-height and terminals cut well back. Nulshock sits above it as a stretched, tube-like display face, so the heading feels engineered while the text stays open and plain sans.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-ugariti: Approachable, first of all, thanks to Noto Sans Ugaritic. Its lowercase nearly reaches cap height, with open mouths like unjoined chalk arcs, while Nulshock above it bends its strokes like copper pipe, technical and bold.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-vai: Noto Sans Vai forms words into solid blocks instead of ragged skylines, with generous space where curves meet stems. Nulshock is the one for stretched, technical display work with its constant pen line, and the body face handles everything quieter.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-vithkuq: Nulshock draws spaghetti-like strokes of one width, stretched out with generous tracking. Noto Sans Vithkuqi follows with open-throated letters and barely any step up to the capitals, so a long passage glides along in a modern, plain sans.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho looks hulking, like thick chalk pressed hard. Nulshock overhead builds its capitals from lines of one constant thickness, so a thin outlined heading rests on a heavy-looking plain sans.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-warang-: Contemporary and tidy, this pairing puts a monoline Nulshock over Noto Sans Warang Citi. And its strongest quality is the text, where words form solid blocks and wide channels lead into every counter.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-yi: Flat lines, wide stance, a technical bite: that is Nulshock, with no swell along any curve. Noto Sans Yi does the quieter job, with a deep midsection and unlatched rounds that make the plain sans text easy to work through.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-zanabaz: Nulshock brings a stretched, technical outline look with no calligraphic swell on any downstroke, and Noto Sans Zanabazar Square soars beneath it. Give the sans-serif body a little extra size, since its wide gaps keep small text crisp.
